exposure: immigrant status (Turkish origin, other immigrant origin, German)
outcome: use of local and regional anaesthesia
cohort: 5445 women giving birth at the Virchow Hospital in 1974, 1984, and 1994
finding: While rates of major obstetric interventions did not differ, immigrant women, particularly those of Turkish origin, received less pain relief and anaesthesia during labor but were more likely to receive oxytocin augmentation compared to German women.
